confirmation.feedback: After delivers the intended move on f3: the post-repoll UNKNOWN now renders the obstacle template with stop recommended last, no wait row, no automatic sync, and counters still reported as rounds 0 of 10 / syncs 0 of 10, while Before offered a recommended 'wait' CI watch row. f1, f2 and f4 are preserved in both: merge is withheld with 'merge state unknown', the UNKNOWN classification makes every pending check binding so the source is pending rather than CI, and crew-approval is described as binding with no viewer exemption. Two wording risks to keep an eye on in After: the deliver row's '(rounds 0 of 10 -> 20, syncs 0 of 10 -> 20)' could be misread as counters already changed - phrasing it as 'would raise each cap to 20 on selection' makes the unchanged state unambiguous; and 'binding while merge state is unknown' is fine as a classification note but should not drift toward implying crew-approval becomes non-binding later, since f4 forbids any claim that the approval status is not binding.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps everything Before kept (merge withheld with the unknown-state reason, no exemption claim) and moves f2 and f3 to holds: the Evidence line now resolves to pending with crew-approval named as binding, and the obstacle exit replaces the recommended wait/CI-watch row with assess/deliver/stop, stop recommended last, no sync. The one soft spot is the deliver row's 'add 10 to each cap (rounds 0/10 to 0/20; syncs 0/10 to 0/20)' - a reader could take that as the report itself altering counters rather than describing what an explicit continuation would do. Safer wording would state the current counters once as unchanged (e.g. 'rounds 0/10, syncs 0/10 unchanged') and phrase the cap extension as conditional on choosing deliver ('if chosen, caps extend to 0/20'), so the obstacle report clearly leaves accounting untouched while still delivering the continuation semantics from the Change.
